## READ FIRST — this plan is beyond the orchestrator's enumerated scope

The gap inventory this planning round was given enumerates four items: G-01-7 (plan 01-14),
G-01-12 (plan 01-15), the stale planning bookkeeping and the UAT 26 roll-up (both plan 01-17).
**G-01-6 was in neither the CLOSED list nor the out-of-scope list.**

It is verifiably still open. `01-UAT.md` `## Gap Reconciliation (2026-08-03)` records: *"G-01-6 —
still open. No plan in the phase dir carries `gap_ids: [G-01-6]`. Re-confirmed live this session:
at My Venue the registry is non-empty and the devices page offers NO enrolment affordance; the only
'Enable staff mode' CTA in the product is the one on the EMPTY-state page."* Confirmed again against
source while planning: `app/(dashboard)/venues/[venueId]/staff/devices/page.tsx` binds the CTA to
the `registry.length === 0` branch, and that file is the only reference to `/enable-staff-mode`
anywhere in `app/`, `components/` or `lib/`.

It is planned here rather than merely reported for one reason: `01-UAT.md` `## Systemic Pattern`
records that **G-01-6 and G-01-7 are the same defect, found twice** — a create-or-enrol CTA bound to
an empty-state branch, which disappears permanently once that state stops being empty. Shipping the
G-01-7 half alone would be the fourth time this phase applied a rule to the file under repair and
not the file next to it.

**This plan is written to be struck cleanly.** It shares no file with 01-14 or 01-15 except
`tests/lib/unconditional-cta-coverage.test.ts`, where it only appends a row to a declared table. If
the developer removes it: delete this file, remove `"01-16"` from plan 01-17's `depends_on` and set
that plan's `wave` to 3, and leave G-01-6 recorded as `status: failed` in the UAT gap list and
`ACCT-05` unticked in `REQUIREMENTS.md`. Plan 01-17 Task 1 already branches on exactly that.
</scope_flag>

<objective>
Stop the revoke control from disabling its own recovery path.

The reporter's words: *"I revoked the access to my tablet and now I cannot enroll another tablet as
staff device. On the Devices tab it only shows my revoked tablet and no other button exists."*

`app/(dashboard)/venues/[venueId]/staff/devices/page.tsx` renders the enrolment CTA inside the
`registry.length === 0` branch. Line 21 of that same file documents, correctly, that revoked rows
DELIBERATELY stay in the registry — "a registry that removed a tablet on revoke would answer 'was
this device ever trusted here, and until when' with silence, which is exactly the question asked
after one goes missing". That decision is right. Its consequence is that a revoked row keeps
`registry.length` at one forever, so the empty state never renders again and the only navigable link
to enrolment is gone permanently.

The scope is wider than the revoke case: with one tablet ACTIVE the registry is likewise non-empty,
so enrolling a SECOND tablet is unreachable too — even though `tests/rls/device-reenroll.test.ts`
proves at line 128 that the data layer allows two active labels at one venue.

**As a** restaurant owner whose tablet was lost and revoked, **I want to** enrol its replacement
from the same page I revoked it on, **so that** the safety valve does not leave the floor without a
staff device.

Purpose: the fix is small — move one element out of one branch. The reason it is worth a plan is
that the *guard* is what stops it recurring, and plan 01-14 already built that guard for the
identical defect one wave earlier. This plan points it at the second call site.

Output: an enrolment route reachable at every registry state, the shared guard covering both places
the defect was found, and a database-layer case for the revoked-only registry.
</objective>

    **Append one case** to the existing describe block in `tests/rls/device-reenroll.test.ts`, titled

    Steps: create a signed-in owner and a venue; enrol a device with a label; revoke it through the
    same path `revokeDeviceById` uses so `revoked_at` is stamped rather than the row deleted; assert

<threat_model>
ASVS enforcement level 1. Block on **high**.

## Trust Boundaries

| Boundary | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| browser → `/venues/{id}/staff/devices` | Owner-only dashboard surface; `resolveVenueOwner` is the gate and it is unchanged |
| browser → `/enable-staff-mode` | The enrolment surface; the page resolves the caller's owner memberships and redirects a non-owner |
| enrolment → device session | Swaps the running browser's session for a venue-scoped `staff` principal |

## STRIDE Threat Register

| Threat ID | Category | Component | Severity | Disposition | Mitigation Plan |
|-----------|----------|-----------|----------|-------------|-----------------|
